findings.evidence: Every proof in the file re-does this unfolding by hand — lines 44-50, 59-65 each chain `ClassGroup.induction`, `ClassGroup.equiv_mk`, `QuotientGroup.congr_mk'`, `Units.ext`. That repeated boilerplate is exactly the missing characteristic lemma.
findings.fix: Add `mulEquiv_mk (f : R ≃+* S) (I : (FractionalIdeal R⁰ (FractionRing R))ˣ) : ClassGroup.mulEquiv f (ClassGroup.mk _ I) = ClassGroup.mk _ (Units.mapEquiv (FractionalIdeal.ringEquivOfRingEquiv _ _ f) I)` as `@[simp]`, and (for the Dedekind `I · σI` step downstream) the corresponding `mulEquiv_mk0`.
findings.issue: No lemma computes `ClassGroup.mulEquiv f (ClassGroup.mk (FractionRing R) I)`, although the docstring (line 19) states the point is to "compute it on ideal classes". Consumers are left with Mathlib's `@[simps!]`-generated `mulEquiv_apply`, which unfolds to `QuotientGroup.congr`/`canonicalEquiv` machinery rather than a class-level statement.

findings.evidence: grep of mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/ClassGroup/Basic.lean shows no hand-written `mulEquiv_apply`/`mulEquiv_symm_apply`; only `@[simps!]` at line 459, which generates lemmas whose LHS is an application, not a bare `MulEquiv`.
findings.issue: `mulEquiv_trans` (line 54) and `mulEquiv_symm` (line 76) are not `@[simp]` while the parallel `mulEquiv_refl` (line 39) is. The docstrings at lines 67-70 and 86-89 justify withholding `simp` only for the *applied* forms, whose LHS the `simps!`-generated `mulEquiv_apply`/`mulEquiv_symm_apply` already own; the unapplied equalities `mulEquiv (f.trans g) = …` and `(mulEquiv f).symm = …` are not reachable by those lemmas and are terminating rewrites to a normal form.

findings.evidence: Lines 71-73 and 90-92 establish the pointwise-companion pattern; line 39's lemma has none.
findings.fix: Add `mulEquiv_refl_apply (x : ClassGroup R) : ClassGroup.mulEquiv (RingEquiv.refl R) x = x := DFunLike.congr_fun mulEquiv_refl x`.
findings.issue: Pointwise forms are supplied for `trans` (line 71) and `symm` (line 90) but not for `refl`, so the most common consumer shape `ClassGroup.mulEquiv (RingEquiv.refl R) x = x` requires a manual `DFunLike.congr_fun`.

summary: The functorial laws are the right surface, but the file omits the characteristic lemma computing `mulEquiv f` on `ClassGroup.mk` — the very thing the module docstring says it needs — and the `@[simp]` annotations are inconsistent across the three laws.
